lessons.title: Make It Look Right: Text, Font, Colour, Gradients and Opacity

objectives.cognitive: Describe what the font-family, color, background-image gradient and opacity properties change on a page.
objectives.affective: Value text that every reader, including readers with low vision, can read.
objectives.psychomotor: Give Juan's site font lists and a gradient header in styles.css and run it in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample files into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 1, 6 and 9, Media checks. Fonts, sizes, spacing, colours, gradients and opacity are not page text; CodeShare checks them with page checks. Only CSS that changes letters (text-transform) or hides an element changes the page text; faded or invisible words stay. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 4 site carries forward in your module project: index.html, projects.html, contact.html and styles.css. This week changes only styles.css. Each step loads its run page and every file that page needs; the boxes show only the rules a step adds or changes.
**Week 5 starts here:** Juan's site has one stylesheet, but his text uses the browser's plain fonts and spacing, and his name is plain navy text on white.

blocks.term: Text, font, colour, gradient and opacity
blocks.markdown: Text and font properties set how words look. font-family names a list of fonts tried in order, ending in a generic family (serif, sans-serif or monospace) that every computer has; font-size, font-weight and font-style set size, boldness and slant. color sets the text colour, written as a name (white), a hex code (#ffffff) or rgb(255, 255, 255). A gradient is a background image that blends colours: background-image: linear-gradient(to right, #13305c, #8a1c55). opacity fades a whole element, from 1 (solid) to 0 (invisible).
A Foundation Day tarpaulin: the letters, their size and their colours are chosen so people can read it from far away; a blended background looks good only if every word still stands out.

rows: The font: the first one the computer has

blocks.markdown: **Media steps:** Steps 1, 6 and 9 run index.html, with Juan's picture, sound and video, files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, these three steps show Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done. The other steps run projects.html or contact.html and are checked automatically.

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 4 site carries forward; this week changes only styles.css. A font-family value is a list: the browser uses the first font the computer has and ends with a generic family (serif, sans-serif or monospace), which every computer has. This step gives body a sans-serif list and the h1 and h2 headings a serif list. Run it unchanged.

lessons.title: Easy to Read: Font Sizes, Spacing and Alignment

objectives.cognitive: Explain how font-size in em, line-height, letter-spacing and text-align make text easier to read.
objectives.affective: Appreciate room on a page that helps classmates read without strain.
objectives.psychomotor: Space and align Juan's header and size his form labels in em.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's header has a gradient, but its words sit on the left, close together, and his paragraph lines are tight.

font-size can be written in px, in em (times the parent's size: 1.1em of 16px is 17.6px) or in rem (times the page's base size). line-height sets the space each line takes (1.5 is one and a half times the font size); letter-spacing adds space between letters; text-align places lines left, center or right; text-decoration draws or removes lines such as underline. Page checks read sizes in px and colours in rgb().
A teacher writing on the whiteboard leaves space between lines and centres the title, so the back row can read it.

blocks.instruction: Readable text has room. This step gives body a line-height of 1.5 (each line takes one and a half times the font size) and turns the h1 into a centred header: capitals, 2px between letters and a line-height of 2, which makes the gradient band taller. Run it unchanged.

lessons.title: Colour with Care: Colour Values, Gradients and Opacity

objectives.cognitive: Write one colour as a name, a hex code and rgb(), and tell what a gradient and opacity do to contrast.
objectives.affective: Choose colours with care so that meaning never depends on colour alone.
objectives.psychomotor: Apply rgb() text colour, a badge gradient and faded small print to Juan's site.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's text is readable, but his colours were picked one at a time, and the small print looks as strong as the rest.

A hex colour is # and six digits (00 to ff for red, green and blue); rgb() gives the same three numbers from 0 to 255, and rgba() adds an alpha from 0 (transparent) to 1 (solid). linear-gradient() runs in a direction (to right; to bottom when none is given) through colours separated by commas; radial-gradient() spreads from the centre. opacity fades the element and everything in it, so its text loses contrast.
Mixing paint for a school mural: two colours blended across a wall make a gradient; adding water thins the paint until the wall shows through, like opacity.

rows: # and six digits: two each for red, green, blue
Each 0 to 255; page checks show this form

blocks.instruction: A colour can be written three ways: a name (white), a hex code (#222222) or rgb(red, green, blue), each from 0 to 255. This step gives body a dark grey written as rgb(34, 34, 34), and replaces the badges' flat yellow with a gradient from light yellow to gold. With no direction, a gradient runs from top to bottom. Run it unchanged.

lessons.title: Can Everyone Read It? Contrast and Gradient Repairs, then Start Your Own

objectives.cognitive: Judge whether a text and background pair reaches 4.5:1 and locate a missing bracket or semicolon.
objectives.affective: Show patience and respect for every reader when checking contrast.
objectives.psychomotor: Repair Juan's broken gradient and unreadable heading, then begin the personal styling.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Browsers show no error for broken CSS, and a page can have every word right and still be unreadable to the eye.

Contrast compares the lightness of text and its background, from 1:1 (none) to 21:1 (black on white). Normal text needs at least 4.5:1; large text (24px, or about 19px bold) at least 3:1. On a gradient, check the text against every colour of the gradient. A browser skips a declaration it cannot read and shows no error; a missing ) can switch off every rule after it.
A jeepney signboard with dark letters on a dark board cannot be read at night, however nice the colours; one missing bracket is like tape over the rest of the signboard.

rows: Juan's name (h1), white on the gradient

blocks.instruction: Broken on purpose: the closing bracket ) of the h1's gradient is missing. The browser reads the rest of the file as part of that value, so every later rule stops. Run it unchanged: no gradient, the white name vanishes on the white page, and the navigation and badges are in small letters.

rows.see: The gradient or a colour is gone; white words vanish on the white page.
rows.means: The value is invalid: a missing comma between colours, a misspelt direction (to rigth) or a colour without #. The whole declaration is skipped.
rows.fix: linear-gradient(to right, #13305c, #8a1c55): commas between parts, # before each colour.

rows.see: The gradient and every rule after it stop working.
rows.means: A ( has no closing ), so the rest of the file is read as part of that value.

rows.see: A heading is dark on the dark gradient and lost its capitals.
rows.means: The ; after its color is missing, so that declaration and the next are skipped.

rows.see: Words cannot be seen, but they are still in the output.
rows.means: Their colour is too close to the background, transparent, or at opacity 0.
rows.fix: Pick a pair of 4.5:1 or more from the contrast chart.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 5: Readable Text and a Gradient Header
performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 4 site carries forward: add this week's rules to your own styles.css.

Give your text font lists, a size, spacing and alignment; choose text colours from the contrast chart; give your h1 a gradient header whose text reaches 4.5:1 against every colour of the gradient; use opacity once without making text hard to read. Use only fonts and colours already on the computer: no @font-face and nothing named in url().

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts. Run code until index.html runs with no error, visit every page with your links, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting. Pictures, sound and video stay online only (Media files).

Thursday: 0–60 minutes, repairs and the Thursday strip; 60–120 minutes, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 minutes, finish and run; 30–105 minutes, five-minute presentations; 105–120 minutes, Friday strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 4 site: every page, the navigation, the frame, the form and styles.css linked from every page.
Give body one font-family list and your headings another, each ending in serif, sans-serif or monospace.
Set a font-size (in em or px) and a line-height that leaves room between lines.
Use text-align and letter-spacing (or text-decoration) on at least one element.
Choose text colours from the contrast chart: at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
Give your h1 a linear-gradient background, with text at 4.5:1 or more against every gradient colour.
Use opacity once, on a picture or on text that keeps 4.5:1.
Colour never carries meaning alone: the words say it too.
Only fonts and colours already on the computer; nothing in url(). No address, phone, birth date, ID numbers or social media.
Run code shows no error; visit every page; press Submit this version, then present your fonts, colours and contrast.
